Driveways that suit Ruislip homes

Much of Ruislip was built in the 1920s and 1930s, when the Metropolitan line arrived and “Metro-land” estates spread out from the High Street and Ruislip Manor. Many of those semi-detached and terraced houses were built before most families owned cars. Today their front gardens are often turned into driveways, or older drives are extended to fit a second car.

A block-paving driveway is a great fit for these homes. You can choose a colour and pattern that suits the brickwork of a 1930s semi, and keep a planted border to soften the front of the house. We use quality materials, including Marshalls bricks, so it looks good for years.

Local things to think about

  • Dropped kerbs: Ruislip is in the London Borough of Hillingdon. If you need a new or wider dropped kerb (vehicle crossover), you will usually need the council's approval first. We can talk you through it [PLACEHOLDER: confirm what help you offer with dropped-kerb applications].
  • Conservation areas: Parts of Ruislip, including around the old village near St Martin's Church and Manor Farm, are in conservation areas [PLACEHOLDER: confirm conservation-area wording]. Extra rules can apply there, so check before planning major front-garden changes.
  • Trees and verges: Many Ruislip roads are tree-lined with grass verges. We will plan your driveway around existing trees and the access to the road.
